role.en: Filipino painter of the Spoliarium; fellow Propagandista and friend of Rizal
role.fil: Pilipinong pintor ng Spoliarium; kapwa Propagandista at kaibigan ni Rizal
role.de: Philippinischer Maler des Spoliarium; Mitstreiter der Propaganda-Bewegung und Freund Rizals

quote.en: So in Luna, we find the shades, the mysterious and the terrible, like an echo of the dark storms of the tropics, its thunderbolts, and the destructive eruption of its volcanoes...
quote.fil: Kaya kay Luna ay matatagpuan natin ang mga anino, ang mahiwaga at ang kakila-kilabot, tila alingawngaw ng madidilim na unos ng tropiko, ng mga kidlat nito, at ng mapaminsalang pagputok ng mga bulkan nito...
quote.de: So finden wir bei Luna die Schatten, das Geheimnisvolle und das Schreckliche, wie ein Echo der dunklen Stürme der Tropen, ihrer Blitze und des zerstörerischen Ausbruchs ihrer Vulkane...

bio.en:
In his imaginings, the Filipino's subjugation under the Spanish colonial government was captured by the brutal experience of the gladiators of Rome, despite being on opposite sides of the world. Known for painting this experience in the Spoliarium, Juan Luna may be recognized as one of the, if not the, most renowned among Filipino painters.

Luna won first prize for this artwork at the Exposicion Nacional de Bellas Artes in Madrid in 1884, when he was 27 years old. Before this, he spent his formative years in his hometown, Badoc, Ilocos Norte. He was born Juan Luna de San Pedro y Novicio on 25 October 1857 to Don Joaquin Luna and Doña Laureana Novicio.

Later on, he enrolled at the Academia de Dibujo y Pintura in Manila. After his dismissal from this school, Filipino painter Maestro Lorenzo Guerrero trained Luna to hone his artistic talents. Maestro Guerrero was also instrumental in convincing Luna's parents to send the young artist to Europe for further studies.

Upon his arrival in Europe in 1877, he enrolled at the Escuela de Pintura at the Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando in Madrid. He was 20 years old then. He then sought the guidance of Don Alejo Vera, a known painter in Madrid, who brought Luna with him to Italy in 1878 when he was commissioned to paint. Vera's mentorship of Luna made the Filipino painter prolific, and during this time he produced Daphne and Cloe, The Death of Cleopatra, The Blind Slave, and the Spoliarium, among many others.

This also became the pathway for Luna's genius to become widely known. The Ayuntamiento de Manila granted him an annual pension of 1,000 pesos for four years, allowing him to continue painting in Italy. After spending several years in Rome, he moved his studio to Paris in 1884.

Nearly a decade later, Luna moved from Paris to Spain in 1893 after being embroiled in a crime of passion that resulted in the death of his wife, Paz Pardo de Tavera, and his mother-in-law, while wounding his brother-in-law, Felix Pardo de Tavera.

He moved back to Manila in 1894. He was then briefly imprisoned for being implicated in the Katipunan revolt in 1896. He spent his latter years, after so many life trials, before dying from a heart attack in Hong Kong on 7 December 1899.

To underscore the friendship of the two reformists, Rizal wrote a biographical profile of Luna, which was published in the La Ilustracion Revista Hispano-Americana. In several instances, Luna's life seems to mirror Rizal's. Both were products of Ateneo Municipal de Manila; young artists—Luna with his paintings and Rizal with his sketches—who sought studies in Europe; became notable Propagandistas; and made their marks in Philippine history through their important works—Luna's Spoliarium and Rizal's Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo.
bio.fil:
Sa kanyang guniguni, ang pagkaalipin ng Pilipino sa ilalim ng kolonyal na pamahalaang Espanyol ay nakuha sa mabangis na karanasan ng mga gladiyador ng Roma, sa kabila ng pagiging magkabilang panig ng daigdig. Kilala sa pagpinta ng karanasang ito sa Spoliarium, maaaring kilalanin si Juan Luna bilang isa sa, kung hindi man ang, pinakatanyag sa mga pintor na Pilipino.

Nanalo si Luna ng unang gantimpala para sa akdang ito sa Exposicion Nacional de Bellas Artes sa Madrid noong 1884, nang siya ay 27 taong gulang. Bago nito, ginugol niya ang kanyang mga taon ng paglaki sa kanyang bayang sinilangan, ang Badoc, Ilocos Norte. Isinilang siya bilang Juan Luna de San Pedro y Novicio noong 25 Oktubre 1857 kina Don Joaquin Luna at Doña Laureana Novicio.

Nang maglaon, nag-aral siya sa Academia de Dibujo y Pintura sa Maynila. Matapos siyang matanggal sa paaralang ito, sinanay siya ng pintor na Pilipinong si Maestro Lorenzo Guerrero upang hasain ang kanyang talento sa sining. Si Maestro Guerrero rin ang naging mahalaga sa paghikayat sa mga magulang ni Luna na ipadala ang batang alagad ng sining sa Europa para sa karagdagang pag-aaral.

Pagdating niya sa Europa noong 1877, nag-aral siya sa Escuela de Pintura ng Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando sa Madrid. Siya ay 20 taong gulang noon. Hiniling niya ang gabay ni Don Alejo Vera, isang kilalang pintor sa Madrid, na nagdala kay Luna sa Italya noong 1878 nang atasan itong magpinta. Ang pagtuturo ni Vera kay Luna ay nagpayabong sa Pilipinong pintor, at sa panahong ito nalikha niya ang Daphne and Cloe, The Death of Cleopatra, The Blind Slave, at ang Spoliarium, bukod sa marami pang iba.

Naging daan din ito upang maging malawak na kilala ang henyo ni Luna. Ipinagkaloob sa kanya ng Ayuntamiento de Manila ang taunang pensiyong 1,000 piso sa loob ng apat na taon, na nagbigay-daan upang magpatuloy siya sa pagpipinta sa Italya. Matapos ang ilang taon sa Roma, inilipat niya ang kanyang estudyo sa Paris noong 1884.

Halos isang dekada ang lumipas, lumipat si Luna mula Paris patungong Espanya noong 1893 matapos masangkot sa isang krimen ng silakbo ng damdamin na ikinamatay ng kanyang asawang si Paz Pardo de Tavera at ng kanyang biyenang babae, at ikinasugat ng kanyang bayaw na si Felix Pardo de Tavera.

Bumalik siya sa Maynila noong 1894. Saglit siyang nabilanggo dahil sa pagkakasangkot sa pag-aalsa ng Katipunan noong 1896. Ginugol niya ang kanyang mga huling taon, matapos ang napakaraming pagsubok sa buhay, bago namatay sa atake sa puso sa Hong Kong noong 7 Disyembre 1899.

Upang bigyang-diin ang pagkakaibigan ng dalawang repormista, sumulat si Rizal ng talambuhay ni Luna, na inilathala sa La Ilustracion Revista Hispano-Americana. Sa ilang pagkakataon, tila sinasalamin ng buhay ni Luna ang buhay ni Rizal. Kapwa sila bunga ng Ateneo Municipal de Manila; mga batang alagad ng sining—si Luna sa kanyang mga pinta at si Rizal sa kanyang mga sketch—na naghangad ng pag-aaral sa Europa; naging kilalang mga Propagandista; at nag-iwan ng bakas sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas sa pamamagitan ng kanilang mahahalagang akda—ang Spoliarium ni Luna at ang Noli Me Tangere at El Filibusterismo ni Rizal.
bio.de:
In seiner Vorstellung fand die Unterwerfung der Filipinos unter die spanische Kolonialregierung ihr Bild in der brutalen Erfahrung der Gladiatoren Roms — obwohl beide Welten weit voneinander entfernt lagen. Bekannt dafür, diese Erfahrung im Spoliarium gemalt zu haben, darf Juan Luna als einer der bekanntesten, wenn nicht als der bekannteste philippinische Maler gelten.

Luna gewann für dieses Werk 1884 den ersten Preis der Exposicion Nacional de Bellas Artes in Madrid, mit 27 Jahren. Zuvor verbrachte er seine prägenden Jahre in seiner Heimatstadt Badoc, Ilocos Norte. Er wurde am 25. Oktober 1857 als Juan Luna de San Pedro y Novicio als Sohn von Don Joaquin Luna und Doña Laureana Novicio geboren.

Später schrieb er sich an der Academia de Dibujo y Pintura in Manila ein. Nach seinem Verweis von dieser Schule bildete der philippinische Maler Maestro Lorenzo Guerrero Luna aus, um sein künstlerisches Talent zu schärfen. Maestro Guerrero war auch maßgeblich daran beteiligt, Lunas Eltern zu überzeugen, den jungen Künstler zum weiteren Studium nach Europa zu schicken.

Nach seiner Ankunft in Europa 1877 schrieb er sich an der Escuela de Pintura der Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando in Madrid ein. Er war damals 20 Jahre alt. Daraufhin suchte er die Anleitung Don Alejo Veras, eines bekannten Madrider Malers, der Luna 1878 nach Italien mitnahm, als er einen Malauftrag erhielt. Veras Mentorschaft machte den philippinischen Maler produktiv, und in dieser Zeit entstanden unter vielen anderen Daphne and Cloe, The Death of Cleopatra, The Blind Slave und das Spoliarium.

Dies wurde auch der Weg, auf dem Lunas Genie weithin bekannt wurde. Das Ayuntamiento de Manila gewährte ihm vier Jahre lang eine Jahrespension von 1.000 Pesos, die es ihm erlaubte, in Italien weiterzumalen. Nach mehreren Jahren in Rom verlegte er sein Atelier 1884 nach Paris.

Fast ein Jahrzehnt später zog Luna 1893 von Paris nach Spanien, nachdem er in ein Eifersuchtsverbrechen verwickelt worden war, bei dem seine Frau Paz Pardo de Tavera und seine Schwiegermutter ums Leben kamen und sein Schwager Felix Pardo de Tavera verwundet wurde.

1894 kehrte er nach Manila zurück. Danach war er kurzzeitig inhaftiert, weil man ihn 1896 mit dem Katipunan-Aufstand in Verbindung brachte. Nach so vielen Prüfungen verbrachte er seine letzten Jahre, bis er am 7. Dezember 1899 in Hongkong einem Herzinfarkt erlag.

Um die Freundschaft der beiden Reformer zu unterstreichen, verfasste Rizal ein biografisches Porträt Lunas, das in der La Ilustracion Revista Hispano-Americana erschien. In mehrfacher Hinsicht scheint Lunas Leben das Rizals zu spiegeln. Beide gingen aus dem Ateneo Municipal de Manila hervor; beide waren junge Künstler — Luna mit seinen Gemälden, Rizal mit seinen Zeichnungen —, die ein Studium in Europa suchten; beide wurden bedeutende Propagandistas; und beide prägten die philippinische Geschichte durch ihre wichtigen Werke — Lunas Spoliarium sowie Rizals Noli Me Tangere und El Filibusterismo.
